=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- Requirement: PR description states "Reclassify `pipeline_failed_without_changes` from `error` → `red`, so a consumer self-test failure is consistently non-blocking regardless of drift." The implementation correctly changes `error` to `red` but the inline comment at `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py` line 323 and the `main()` comment at line 834 both describe the `red` outcome as "self-test failed," which is narrower than what the code actually handles. The code path `pipeline_green == False` catches any render, lint, or self_test stage failure — not only self-test. The comment should reflect this broader condition.
  Expected change site: `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py` lines 323-334 (process_repository comment) and lines 830-836 (main() comment)
  Evidence of absence: The diff at `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py` line 323 introduces the comment "Consumer self-test failed and the rendered assets matched the committed ones (no drift)." The actual conditional is `if not has_changes: if pipeline_green: ... else:` where `pipeline_green` is set to `False` when any of render, lint, or self_test fails in `_run_refresh_pipeline` (line 312, line 435). Similarly, the `main()` comment at line 834 says "`red` (self-test failed)" but `red` is assigned at both line 337 (no-drift pipeline failure, any stage) and line 344 (drift-present pipeline failure, any stage).
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: PR description lists "`README.md` — document that a consumer self-test failure is `red` whether or not assets drifted, and that only mechanism errors gate the release smoke." The README update at line 1697 says "This is a consumer self-test failure (same severity class as a drift-present `red`)" — the wording "consumer self-test failure" implies only the self_test stage is covered, while the code classifies any pipeline stage failure without drift as `red`. The documentation should use broader language matching the actual behavior.
  Expected change site: `README.md` lines 1696-1699
  Evidence of absence: README diff at line 1697 reads "This is a consumer self-test failure" but `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py` line 322 sets `pipeline_green` from all three stages (render, lint, self_test — lines 431-435 in `_run_refresh_pipeline`), and any stage failure triggers the `red` outcome at line 337.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- File: scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py
  Line or code reference: process_repository:323-338 (comment) and _run_refresh_pipeline:682-710
  Problem: The added comment and the parallel README update repeatedly describe the `pipeline_failed_without_changes` path as exclusively a “consumer self-test failure”. In reality the `else:` branch after `has_changes == False` is reached for *any* stage (`render`, `lint`, or `self_test`) that returns non-zero while leaving the working tree clean.
  Why it fails at runtime: When render or lint fails without drift the diagnostic and documentation will misdirect operators to look only at the self-test stage, creating a latent correctness gap in observability and debugging.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: “a consumer self-test failure is `red` whether or not the assets drifted” and “Pipeline failure with no file diff: records `red` with the `pipeline_failed_without_changes` diagnostic. This is a consumer self-test failure...”
  Expected change site: README.md:1696-1700 and scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:323-338 (new comment block)
  Evidence of absence: Both the prose and the code comment narrow the condition to “self-test” while the actual control-flow (`if not has_changes: … else: … if not pipeline_green`) covers any pipeline stage failure that produces a clean git status. The PR description and new test correctly use the broader semantics; the delivered documentation does not.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
